findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are hardcoded in plaintext in the Lambda function's environment variables, making them readable to anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration permissions and committing them to version control.

The Lambda function's environment variables are not encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key (no kms_key_arn is set), so sensitive values are only protected by the AWS-managed default key with no explicit key policy or rotation control.
The function uses the nodejs12.x runtime, which is end-of-life and no longer receives security patches from AWS.
No code_signing_config_arn is configured, so the deployment package is not signature-validated and tampering with the artefact between build and deployment would go undetected.

The function has no vpc_config, so it runs outside any customer VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security group or subnet-level egress control, providing a potential data exfiltration path.
